My land is 1.7 mu — all of it goes to maize, same as every year. My son is in the city, so it's just me and my wife. I can't manage much more than this anyway at my age, and honestly the maize doesn't need me to reinvent anything. I've been doing this for 50 years on this same soil. I know what it needs.

I'll buy hybrid seed from the township supply cooperative, same brand I've used the last few years — Xianyu or Zhengdan. The yield is better, and I'm not going back to traditional seed. That was a long time ago.

For fertilizer, I'll put down compound fertilizer as the base before planting, then come back with urea when the stalks reach my knee at jointing stage. That's always worked. I'll do maybe 16 kg nitrogen per mu total, split between base and top-dress. Phosphorus and potassium I'll put in at planting — about 6 kg each. I don't test the soil; I go by how the leaves look and what I've learned over the years.

I have the well, so I won't worry about drought. I'll irrigate before seeding to get good germination, again at jointing, and once more at tasseling if the sky stays dry. Three times is usually enough.

I'll rotary till after I prep the bed — clears the old stubble, easy on me. No-till is what the government people say now, but rotary is what I know and my back can still handle the tractor rental.

Two pesticide sprays: herbicide right after emergence, and I'll watch for corn borer in July — spray if I see the damage.

I expect around 550 jin per mu. Not a big field, but it'll be enough grain for the house and a little to sell.
